issue.body:
My clang-cl.exe hangs for the following source code. In about 1 out of 10 runs the compilation is successful.

Environment: Windows 10 64-bit, Visual Studio 2022
Clang 19.1.0-rc2, prebuilt (LLVM-19.1.0-rc2-Windows-X64.tar.xz)
Clang 20.0.0, 64-bit, local debug build

`clang-cl.exe /nologo /MTd /EHa main.cxx`

------------------------------------------------------------------------------

[main.cxx]

```
#include <map>
#include <cassert>

void Foo (std::map<int,int> const &mapFoo,
          std::size_t const bar)
{
  auto cur = mapFoo.find(0);
  assert(bar>=0);
}

int main ()
{
  std::map<int,int> M;
  
  Foo (M, 7);
}
```

comments.author: glebov-andrey
comments.body:
It looks like this is related to the `/EHa` flag which is added by OpenCV. With `/EHsc` the issue goes away.
#106915 looks like it may be related - it's in the same pass, and also while building OpenCV (I guess not that many projects enable `/EHa`).
#83450 also looks like it could be the same issue.

comments.author: R-Goc
comments.body: What is actually being built in my issue (#106915) is protobufs,, as part of opencv. Which are more common than OpenCV, I'd say. Also the reason I didn't even attempt a minimal reproduction(over 350k LOC in that one file), so seeing this issue is good. I can confirm that it will freeze on the linking step, both with Thin and Full LTO.

comments.author: R-Goc
comments.body: Now trying your reproduction, both clang 18.1.8 and 20.0.0 hang without LTO, but don't signal. The protobufs example signals without assertions. However with your reproduction the hang only happens for me when linking with the debug library /MTd /MDd and works on /MT and /MD, unlike the protobufs. Indeed changing to /EHsc fixes it. However, this doesn't reproduce the signal for me. Both with and without LTO it only hangs. I'm building a debug version of LLVM now to see if it will catch an assert.

comments.author: R-Goc
comments.body: Could you see if the descriptor I sent signals for you? Not sure if it would compile for you though. It prints that it includes part of protobufs. For me after removing -fasync-exceptions from the compilation command it no longer signals.  However I am unable to make it fail without a debug runtime on your example. The protobufs example compiles for me with icx-cl with these compile commands, and hangs with 18.1.8, but doesn't signal. I am also able to make your example hang passing -fasync-exceptions -fexceptions -fcxx-exceptions directly to the clang driver with -Xclang. By replicating the bahavior of /MTd and passing -D_DEBUG compilation also fails with /MT but that's not exactly productive.

comments.author: R-Goc
comments.body: However despite the differences the same assert gets triggered, and the stack trace is basically identical, with a new debug build. Also for whatever reason I am unable to use lldb or gdb on this. They don't catch the signal, and the process just terminates.

comments.author: glebov-andrey
comments.body:
> What is actually being built in my issue (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/106915) is protobufs,, as part of opencv. Which are more common than OpenCV, I'd say.

The reason OpenCV is important here is that it adds the `/EHa` flag. I'm pretty sure `protobuf` (I did a quick search through its `main`) doesn't add any `/EH` flags itself.

> Now trying your reproduction, both clang 18.1.8 and 20.0.0 hang without LTO, but don't signal.

Regarding the hanging, it's probably just some kind of UB which results in an infinite loop. Because at least for me, both Release+Assertions and Debug builds fail the assertion every time.
I actually also got a hang once during a debug build with the Release (no assertions) build of Clang, however it only happened once. On the other hand the ThinLTO release build of OpenCV (with the same build of Clang) always hangs.

> Could you see if the descriptor I sent signals for you? Not sure if it would compile for you though. It prints that it includes part of protobufs. For me after removing -fasync-exceptions from the compilation command it no longer signals.

Yes, it asserts in the same way for me with `-fasync-exceptions`, and succeeds without it.

Regarding debug/release runtimes - the only thing which the runtime flag controls during compilation (as far as I can tell from driver arguments) are definitions. And since our examples are preprocessed, these flags don't actually make a difference.
What I can say, is that on my end, building with the `/MD` runtime also triggers an assertion, both at compile time (w/o LTO) and at link time (w/ ThinLTO).
